description_en: This archaeological site contains two stone lion sculptures from the 12th to 15th centuries. They are in the heart of Dullu, north-east of the former king's palace (destroyed by Maoists in April 2002 CE, cf. Lecomte-Tilouine 2009b). The sculptures are placed separately and are given very different treatment. One of two lions (DLK0380-001), known as the 'Dullu lion', is painted and placed on a cemented platform in front of the Vijayabhagavatī Mandira. It is facing south-east. A wooden sacrificial post stands in front of the cemented platform. Between 2014 CE and 2022 CE, a metal fence was built around the platform.The "Sinja lion' is the name given to the second lion (DLK0380-002). It is located near the Patangini Devala (DLK0290), north-east of the 'Dullu lion' (-001). The statue was one meter away from the 13th-15th century temples (Patangini Devala and Vijayabhagavatī Mandira) when it was surveyed in 2014 CE. It has been lying outside the temple compound, amidst trash, since the construction of a wall around the monuments. The style of the two objects is similar to that of other stone lions discovered at royal sites of the Khaśa Malla kings, such as in Sinja, Kanakāsundarī Mandira (JUM043) and 'Sāhubaḍā archaeological artefacts' (JUM0520). As previously stated, these lions date from the 12th-15th centuries, which corresponds to the Khaśa Malla era (12th-14th centuries) and the Kalyāl dynasty of Jumla, which succeeded the latter (Andolfatto 2019). The Dullu stone lions must have been carved around the same time as the Patangini Devala (DLK0290). The lack of consideration given to the 'Sinja lion' was already noted by Marie Lecomte-Tilouine who reported the traditional origin of the statues' names as follows: 'It [the 'Sinja lion] is said to have come from Sinja to fight itsalter egofrom Dullu, to have been defeated and to have remained since then in this vanquish position.' (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009a, p. 255).
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
identified_threats: Plants, Water damages, Other, Road widening, Erosion, Encroachment
